about: It's 2:07 AM, it's over, and your body has already started reacting. This is what the research says happens inside you over the next 24 hours: the adrenaline alarm, the cortisol wave you keep topping up, why your brain treats heartbreak partly like physical pain, and why the urge to text her feels so reasonable.

No scientist has tracked a man hour by hour on the night it ended. This video puts two kinds of research side by side: what bodies do in the hours after a serious shock, and brain scans of people who had been left. Treat it as a map, not a stopwatch.

about: It's 1:40 AM, you've had four beers, and the message to your ex is typed out. It's honest. It's well put. It might even be a bit funny. By 11 the next morning it reads very differently.

This episode follows one night hour by hour and puts the research next to it: why a few beers calm you down at the pub and wind you up at home, how alcohol narrows your attention to the loudest thing in the room, why stopping yourself gets harder than starting, why you feel sober before your brakes come back, and why the message felt brilliant when you sent it.

Nobody has studied men texting their exes at 2 AM after four beers. These are lab and survey studies about attention, self-control, sleep and regret, put together. Treat it as a map, not a record of your night.
